# Import a .env file and run your app

Tested with Dopbase **0.1.8 on macOS ARM64**, using separate local demo instances on ports 18840 and 19000. Linux uses the same CLI commands but was not replayed for this guide. Generated IDs, timestamps, and file paths will differ. Paths and setup tokens are redacted below.

Start with [the installation guide](https://github.com/dopbase/dopbase/discussions/61). Keep its server running and use the same client terminal. In any new terminal, restore `DOPBASE_DATA_DIR` to `$HOME/.dopbase-discussion-client` before running these commands.

This example imports two dummy values, runs a command with them, previews an update, and proves that merge preserves an existing key.

## Create the example file

Use a new directory:

```bash
mkdir dopbase-discussion-demo
cd dopbase-discussion-demo
cat > .env <<'EOF'
APP_NAME=discussion-demo
DEMO_API_KEY=demo-only-not-a-real-key
EOF
```

These commands print no output on success. The demo key is not a credential. Keep real `.env` files out of source control and public posts.

## Create the project and environment

```bash
dopbase init discussion-demo/development --from .env
```

```text
Initialized discussion-demo/development.
Project ID:      <PROJECT_ID>
Environment ID:  env_856343
Secrets:         2
```

`Secrets: 2` confirms two entries were imported. The environment ID is generated by the server; yours will differ. The explicit command keeps the input file.

List the records:

```bash
dopbase secret list discussion-demo/development
```

```text
KEY            VERSION   UPDATED
APP_NAME       1         2026-10-02 01:57 UTC
DEMO_API_KEY   1         2026-10-02 01:57 UTC

2 secret(s)
```

The table shows names, versions, and update times. It does not reveal values.

## Verify process injection

```bash
dopbase run discussion-demo/development -- \
  sh -c 'test "$APP_NAME" = "discussion-demo" && echo "Environment loaded"'
```

```text
Dopbase: discussion-demo/development (env_856343), 2 key(s), source=live
Environment loaded
```

The first line is Dopbase's diagnostic on stderr. `Environment loaded` is the child command's stdout. Its assertion confirms the expected variable reached the process. The application does not need a newly exported `.env` file.

For your application, replace the `sh` command with its startup command, such as `npm start`. That command's own output will depend on the application.

## Preview an update

Create a second file:

```bash
cat > update.env <<'EOF'
APP_NAME=discussion-demo-updated
NEW_FEATURE_FLAG=true
EOF
```

File creation prints no output. Preview the import:

```bash
dopbase import discussion-demo/development update.env --dry-run
```

```text
Dry run complete. No changes were applied.
Mode:       merge
Added:      1
Updated:    1
Unchanged:  0
Deleted:    0
```

One new key would be added and one existing key would change. No key would be deleted. `Unchanged: 0` counts unchanged entries from this input file; the omitted `DEMO_API_KEY` remains untouched.

Prove the preview did not change the original value:

```bash
dopbase run discussion-demo/development -- \
  sh -c 'test "$APP_NAME" = "discussion-demo" && echo "Environment loaded"'
```

```text
Dopbase: discussion-demo/development (env_856343), 2 key(s), source=live
Environment loaded
```

## Apply and verify the update

```bash
dopbase import discussion-demo/development update.env
```

```text
Imported secrets into discussion-demo/development.
Mode:       merge
Added:      1
Updated:    1
Unchanged:  0
Deleted:    0
```

Check the changed value, the added flag, and the original dummy key without printing any value:

```bash
dopbase run discussion-demo/development -- sh -c '
  test "$APP_NAME" = "discussion-demo-updated" &&
  test "$NEW_FEATURE_FLAG" = "true" &&
  test "$DEMO_API_KEY" = "demo-only-not-a-real-key" &&
  echo "Update verified; existing key preserved"'
```

```text
Dopbase: discussion-demo/development (env_856343), 3 key(s), source=live
Update verified; existing key preserved
```

The success message requires all three assertions to pass. List the metadata again:

```bash
dopbase secret list discussion-demo/development
```

```text
KEY                VERSION   UPDATED
APP_NAME           2         2026-10-02 01:57 UTC
DEMO_API_KEY       1         2026-10-02 01:57 UTC
NEW_FEATURE_FLAG   1         2026-10-02 01:57 UTC

3 secret(s)
```

`APP_NAME` is now version 2. The original key remains version 1 and the new flag starts at version 1.

## Try guided setup

Use another new directory and a new project name:

```bash
mkdir ../dopbase-guided-demo
cd ../dopbase-guided-demo
cat > .env <<'EOF'
APP_NAME=guided-demo
DEMO_API_KEY=demo-only-not-a-real-key
EOF
dopbase init
```

The directory and file commands are silent on success. Captured `init` interaction below has terminal redraws removed:

```text
.env found

2 variables detected
1 appears sensitive
1 appears non-sensitive

? Import into Dopbase? Yes
? Project/environment (for example payment-service/local): guided-demo/development
✓ Imported 2 variables into guided-demo/development.
✓ Secrets encrypted.
? Delete .env now? No
Warning: .env was kept. Do not commit it.

Run your application with:

  dopbase run guided-demo/development -- <your-command>
```

Choose No for this exercise. The deletion prompt defaults to Yes; read it before confirming. Classification uses variable names, and both entries are imported.

## If the project already exists

Repeating the explicit `init` command produces:

```text
Error: PROJECT_ALREADY_EXISTS: A project with this name already exists.
```

Use `dopbase import` to update an existing environment. To repeat project creation, choose a new project name.

## Cleanup

The example input files contain only dummy values. In each demo directory, remove the `.env` file; also remove `update.env` from the first directory. Removing those files does not delete the server's records. Stop the server with Ctrl+C when finished.

Continue with [connection settings and environment defaults](https://github.com/dopbase/dopbase/discussions/63). What application command are you trying to run with Dopbase?
